methods: evaluating at roots of the divisor
statement: Find the remainder when $x^{4}+px^{3}+qx^{2}+rx+s$ is divided by $x^{2}-1$. Hence determine the condition on $p,q,r,s$ for $x^{2}-1$ to be a factor of the quartic.
solution: The remainder on division by a quadratic is at most linear, so write $x^{4}+px^{3}+qx^{2}+rx+s=(x^{2}-1)Q(x)+Ax+B$. Substituting $x=1$ gives $1+p+q+r+s=A+B$. Substituting $x=-1$ gives $1-p+q-r+s=-A+B$. Adding yields $2(1+q+s)=2B$, so $B=1+q+s$. Subtracting yields $2(p+r)=2A$, so $A=p+r$. The remainder is therefore $(p+r)x+(1+q+s)$. For $x^{2}-1$ to be a factor the remainder must vanish, giving $p+r=0$ and $1+q+s=0$, i.e. $r=-p$ and $s=-q-1$.
hints: The remainder has the form Ax+B.
Plug in x=1 and x=-1 (the roots of x^2-1).
Set the remainder to zero for divisibility.
